title: merge-many then factor reusable Mirror capability atoms
hypothesis: A shared capability atom basis fit to merged source deltas recovers individual tasks and their compositions at lower complete bytes than DARE/DELLA sparse controls, beyond native PCA/shared-basis coding.
physical_object: shared basis learned from a bank of source task deltas
mirror_coordinate: per-task sparse coefficient vector over shared capability atoms
logical_multiplicity: 24 individual synthetic source functions and pairwise composed functions

development.selection_metric: held-out task and composition NRMSE, complete serialized bytes

fresh.reason: frozen development gate decides whether audit is opened

success_gate: Held-out individual and pair-composition NRMSE <=0.05, >=25% complete bank byte savings versus independent and both sparse controls, and improvement over native PCA at matched bytes.
failure_gate: Quality/byte miss or exact native PCA/shared-coordinate alias is FAIL for this synthetic Mirror-specific mechanism hypothesis.
boundaries: Synthetic deltas only; no pretrained model, real tasks or natural quality.
DARE/DELLA/TIES are simplified synthetic controls, not complete algorithm reproductions.
No audit/fresh task identities are opened after development FAIL.
